hero.tagline: Frontend engineer. Thoughtful interfaces. AI tools.
hero.summary: I build maintainable web interfaces and complex PDF/canvas interactions. With 12 years in software engineering and around six years of frontend technical leadership, I’m extending that foundation into AI agent tools and model integration.

projects.description:
### Problem
Document management workflows needed PDF rendering and interactive annotation, highlighting, and drawing within a web interface. Typical documents contained 10-20 pages and were 15-20 MB.

### My contribution
Led six frontend engineers while developing complex PDF/canvas interactions hands-on with Vue 3 and TypeScript.

### Technical decisions
Combined PDF.js document rendering with Konva.js for an editable interaction layer. Built a PDF-processing core and investigated rendering bottlenecks around the document sizes used by the product.

### Trade-offs
The custom interaction layer gave control over editing behavior while adding coordination work between PDF rendering and canvas overlays.

### Outcome
Delivered PDF rendering, annotation, highlighting, and drawing features for a document management product.

### Problem
Coding agents lose context between sessions. Large instruction files consume context even when most of their content is irrelevant to the current task.

### My contribution
Built a Python CLI and shared stdio MCP server for persistent, workspace-scoped notes, traces, and lessons across coding assistants.

### Technical decisions
Combined SQLite FTS5/BM25 full-text search, agent-supplied keywords, entity-based ranking, and evidence links. Implemented normalized-content deduplication, import/export, and agent configuration support. Storage and retrieval run locally, with no LLM or network call on the recall path.

### Trade-offs
Retrieval is lexical, not embedding-based semantic search. Keyword quality and fallback behavior affect results. A bilingual query fixture evaluates recall@k, mean reciprocal rank (MRR), and off-corpus behavior; these are fixture-based evaluations, not production adoption metrics.

### Outcome
Delivered one local memory interface shared by Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, and Kiro, with inspectable retrieval behavior and documented limits.

### Problem
Producing Vietnamese IVR greetings and menus requires script preparation, voice generation, timing controls, and review of missing or mispronounced words.

### My contribution
Built a local web application and CLI integrating edge-tts and a pretrained F5-TTS model for reference-conditioned, zero-shot speech generation. The project performs no model training or fine-tuning.

### Technical decisions
A Node.js server orchestrates Python inference and FFmpeg processing. A resident worker reuses the loaded F5-TTS checkpoint and releases it after inactivity. The pipeline normalizes Vietnamese numbers, chunks long text, and assembles MP3/WAV output.

### Trade-offs
Speech generation remains variable. Optional Whisper transcription checks the output against the script, triggers bounded retries, and retains the best-matching result; users can review and regenerate individual lines. The selected checkpoint is restricted to non-commercial use and reference voices require appropriate rights.

### Outcome
Delivered a local prototype with per-line preview, regeneration, transcript review, saved jobs, and audio export, demonstrating model integration and audio-workflow engineering.
